articles.title: Why China’s reusable rocket breakthrough matters for the PLA’s ‘kill chain’
articles.summary: China's recent success in recovering reusable rockets marks a significant advancement in its aerospace capabilities, potentially enhancing the People's Liberation Army's operational effectiveness by bolstering the resilience of its satellite-supported "kill chain" in combat scenarios. This breakthrough not only underscores China's growing technological prowess but also raises strategic implications for military engagements in the region.

articles.title: The fog of hunger
articles.summary:
• Societal norms instill in women a lifelong struggle with appetite suppression, leading to a complex relationship with food.  
• The psychological toll of hunger restriction manifests as a cognitive fog, obscuring clarity and self-perception.  
• This internalized discipline often results in a paradox where the pursuit of control over one's body leads to greater disempowerment.  
• The essay invites reflection on how cultural expectations shape not just eating habits, but broader aspects of identity and agency.  
• Ultimately, it challenges us to reconsider the implications of appetite regulation on mental health and personal freedom.

articles.title: China clears Geely for landmark satellite IoT test to spur commercial space sector
articles.summary: China's approval of Geely's satellite IoT trial marks a pivotal moment for the country's commercial space sector, signaling a significant shift towards privatization and innovation in satellite communications. This breakthrough not only enhances Geely's technological ambitions but also opens the floodgates for private investment in a rapidly evolving market.
